headline: Liquor board fines fish market restaurant for serving a minor

meeting.body: Liquor Board Fines Pāʻia Fish Market $5,000 for Serving Minor
meeting.summary: The board fined a fish market restaurant $2,000 and $3,000 on two counts after a cashier served beer to a 19-year-old decoy.
meeting.recap: The board heard a case against a fish market restaurant at 110 Hāna Highway.[[0:00:00]] No one from the restaurant showed up when the case was called.[[0:01:18]] The chair said the board would enter a default, meaning it would go ahead without the business.[[0:02:33]] On June 27th, 2025, the Department of Liquor Control sent underage decoys into the restaurant.[[0:02:52]] A cashier checked a 19-year-old decoy's real Hawaiʻi ID and still served her a beer.[[0:03:12]] The business faced three counts, including serving liquor to a minor and not properly checking ID.[[0:04:35]] The department said the business had a prior offense for serving a minor in the early 2000s.[[0:06:16]] The department recommended a $2,000 fine on each of the first two counts and no penalty on count three.[[0:06:31]] The board voted unanimously to go into closed session, a private discussion, to deliberate.[[0:06:47]] A member moved to fine the business $2,000 on count one, $3,000 on count two, and nothing on count three.[[0:08:14]] The motion passed unanimously.[[0:09:15]] Payment of the fines will be due when the business is notified.[[0:09:27]]
decided: The board voted unanimously to recess open session and go into closed session to deliberate.
The board voted unanimously to fine the business $2,000 on count one and $3,000 on count two, with no further penalty on count three.
meeting.next: The business's payment will be due when it is notified.

moments.q: No one appears for the business
The department lays out the decoy case
